--- title: "[GaussianLS]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Gaussian location-scale family for GAMLSS. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L11-L276){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GaussianLS() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `GaussianLS` extends the plain `Gaussian` family to allow both the mean `mu` and the standard deviation `sigma` to vary smoothly with covariates, rather than assuming constant variance. Use it when a continuous, approximately symmetric response shows heteroscedasticity — for example, when the spread of measurements grows or shrinks over the range of a predictor — and you want the model to capture that varying spread rather than average it away. Each parameter has its own additive predictor and its own link function: `mu` uses the identity link (as in `Gaussian`), and `sigma` uses the log link, which keeps the fitted standard deviation positive. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-name} : `GaussianLS` takes no constructor arguments; both `mu` and `sigma` are modeled entirely through the formulas supplied to `GAMLSS`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The two parameters use distinct link functions: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \mu \qquad \text{(identity)}, \qquad g_{\sigma}(\sigma) = \log(\sigma). $$ The response density is the ordinary Gaussian density evaluated at the fitted, observation- specific `mu` and `sigma`: $$ f(y \mid \mu, \sigma) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right), $$ so the log-likelihood contribution for a single observation is $\ell_i = -\log\sigma_i - \tfrac{1}{2}\log(2\pi) - \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\frac{y_i - \mu_i}{\sigma_i}\right)^2$. Unlike `Gaussian`, there is no separate scale parameter to estimate: `sigma` itself is the quantity being modeled by its own smooth predictor. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS with a smoothly varying mean and standard deviation: ::: {#eed77d9c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.sin(x) sigma = 0.2 + 0.3 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) y = rng.normal(mu, sigma) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "sigma": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.GaussianLS(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: GaussianLS(mu=identity, sigma=log) N obs: 300 Global deviance: 271.2831 AIC: 297.3004 BIC: 345.4816 Log-likelihood: -135.6416 Converged: True (4 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 6.63 Smooth 1: edf = 5.63 --- sigma --- EDF total: 6.38 Smooth 1: edf = 5.38 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
parameter_names Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `GaussianLS`.
### [parameter_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `GaussianLS`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [parameter_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description

dl_dtheta() First derivative of the Gaussian log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `sigma`.
initialize() Starting values for `mu` and `sigma` from the raw response.

### [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Expected Fisher information for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L186-L215){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python d2l_dtheta2(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For the Gaussian distribution these expected information terms do not depend on `y`: $$ -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = \frac{1}{\sigma^2}, \qquad -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right] = \frac{2}{\sigma^2}. $$ ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)` (unused, kept for interface consistency). [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} First derivative of the Gaussian log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L156-L184){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python dl_dtheta(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The score functions are $$ \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \frac{y - \mu}{\sigma^2}, \qquad \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma} = -\frac{1}{\sigma} + \frac{(y-\mu)^2}{\sigma^3}. $$ ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivatives, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu` and `sigma` from the raw response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L237-L256){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `mu` is initialized at the observed values themselves and `sigma` at the sample standard deviation of `y`, constant across observations. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `{"mu": y.copy(), "sigma": }`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the link function for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L88-L109){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `mu` uses the identity link and `sigma` uses the log link, so that `sigma`'s additive predictor is unconstrained while the fitted standard deviation stays positive after applying `link_inverse`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linked values: `values` unchanged for `"mu"`, `log(values)` for `"sigma"`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the link function for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L133-L154){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For the identity link, $d\eta/d\mu = 1$; for the log link, $d\eta/d\sigma = 1/\sigma$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale at which to evaluate the derivative, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An array of ones for `"mu"`, or `1 / values` for `"sigma"`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse link for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L111-L131){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(param, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Maps the additive predictor `eta` back to the natural scale: unchanged for `mu` (identity link), exponentiated for `sigma` (log link) so it stays positive. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Additive predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `eta` unchanged for `"mu"`, `exp(eta)` for `"sigma"`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total Gaussian log-likelihood at the current `mu` and `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L217-L235){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, params) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate response values from `Normal(mu, sigma)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian_ls.py#L258-L273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(params, rng) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A NumPy random generator used to draw the simulated values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, shape `(n,)`. :::
